title: Quentin and the Vow
premise: Rafael Joubert, a ghostwriter who has built a career out of other people's truths while burying her own, is hired to write the memoirs of celebrated novelist Edmund Vale—her former mentor, and the man she loved and left eleven years ago. When a lost letter she wrote him the night she vanished resurfaces in his archives, Edmund realizes the anonymous voice behind his new memoir is the woman who once promised to stay. As deadline pressure, a predatory publisher, and Edmund's own failing memory close in, Rafael must decide whether to claim her name on the page and in his life, or disappear again. She chooses him, signing her first book under her own name as his memory begins to fail—love claimed just in time, and grief arriving on schedule.
about_author: Vesper Vane is the pen name of a former publishing insider who spent a decade writing other people's stories before claiming her own. She lives in a coastal town in Brittany, where she collects unsent letters and writes at dawn.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV. Establish her invisible life: celebrated ghostwriter, no byline, no attachments, apartment stripped of personal history. She accepts a lucrative, secret contract to ghostwrite Edmund Vale's memoirs, telling herself the past is past. Emotional beat: controlled detachment masking old wounds.

chapters.title: House of a Famous Man
chapters.summary: Rafael arrives at Edmund's cliffside house in Brittany for their first interview session. He doesn't know her identity; she wears a professional mask. The house is full of the life she abandoned. Emotional beat: dread braided with longing, every room a landmine.

chapters.title: Eleven Years, Compressed
chapters.summary: Rafael's POV, flashback woven through present interviews. How they met: a young editor and her brilliant, married mentor; the affair; the night she fled after writing a letter she never sent—or thought she never sent. Emotional beat: the past tense cracking open.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Rafael, cataloging Edmund's papers for the memoir, finds a box of unsent correspondence—and her own letter, postmarked eleven years ago, never delivered, returned unopened. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: vertigo; the past is not past at all.

chapters.title: What the Letter Said
chapters.summary: Rafael rereads her own words: love, apology, a vow to return if he ever asked. She hides the letter, terrified he'll find it. Edmund's POV briefly: he senses his ghostwriter is familiar, haunted by her cadences. Emotional beat: secrecy as self-protection beginning to fail.

chapters.title: Interviews and Near Misses
chapters.summary: Sessions continue. Edmund recounts the year she left without knowing he's describing her; Rafael transcribes her own disappearance in third person. A slip—she quotes something only the letter contained. Emotional beat: intimacy rebuilt on a lie, unbearable and addictive.

chapters.title: The Rival's Manuscript
chapters.summary: Rafael's agent reveals the publisher also wants a competing tell-all by Edmund's estranged daughter, Camille, and pressures Rafael for damaging material. Rafael refuses; her contract—and career—is threatened. Emotional beat: the career that saved everything now demanding her betrayal.

chapters.title: Camille
chapters.summary: Camille arrives at the house, sharp and grieving, suspicious of the anonymous ghostwriter. She and Rafael circle each other; Camille reveals Edmund's memory is deteriorating—early dementia, hidden from the public. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: fear that time, not people, is the true rival.

chapters.title: The Day He Forgot
chapters.summary: Edmund mistakes Rafael for someone from his past—perhaps for her, calling her by a pet name no stranger would know. Rafael holds his hand and says nothing. POV alternates. Emotional beat: tenderness and guilt fused; the clock now audible.

chapters.title: A Vow Remembered
chapters.summary: Edmund, in a lucid evening, tells the story of a woman who promised to come back, and says he's been waiting eleven years to be asked. Rafael nearly confesses; Camille interrupts. Emotional beat: the confession rising like a tide and forced back.

chapters.title: The Publisher's Leverage
chapters.summary: The publisher threatens to expose the memoir's ghostwriter and Edmund's diagnosis unless Rafael delivers scandal. Rafael realizes the letter, if found, could prove everything—her identity, her love, her desertion. Emotional beat: cornered; duty and love fully at war.

chapters.title: Stolen Pages
chapters.summary: Rafael discovers someone has been through the archive; the letter is missing. Suspecting Camille, she confronts her. Camille denies it but reveals she knows the ghostwriter's identity—she recognized Rafael's prose from an old magazine. Emotional beat: the mask torn, ally or adversary unresolved.

chapters.title: Midnight on the Cliff Path
chapters.summary: Edmund, disoriented at night, walks the cliff path he and Rafael once walked. Rafael finds him; in the fog he speaks clearly, telling her he knows who she is—has known for weeks—and asks why she never came back. Emotional beat: the truth half-said, suspended over the sea.

chapters.title: The Answer He Deserved
chapters.summary: Rafael finally tells Edmund everything: fear, ambition, shame, the letter she believed unsent. He confesses he found it years ago and kept it, unable to decide whether her silence was mercy or cruelty. Emotional beat: devastating mutual honesty; love no longer deniable.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: The publisher sets a final ultimatum: deliver the exposé chapters or lose the contract, the advance, and the career. Rafael, with Edmund's blessing, begins writing the true memoir—naming herself as its author and its subject. Emotional beat: choosing the person over the profession.

chapters.title: Camille's Choice
chapters.summary: Camille, holding the missing letter (she took it to protect her father), reads it at last. Instead of weaponizing it, she gives it back and agrees to help publish the truth—including her own grief. Emotional beat: reconciliation; the rival becomes family.

chapters.title: The Publisher Strikes
chapters.summary: The publisher leaks Edmund's diagnosis and the ghostwriting arrangement, framing Rafael as a fraud. The literary world erupts; her reputation, built on invisibility, is destroyed in public. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: the career that saved everything now burning.

chapters.title: What Cannot Be Ghostwritten
chapters.summary: In the wreckage, Edmund's lucidity narrows to windows. He asks Rafael to read him the finished memoir aloud; she reads their story to him as though it were a stranger's, and he corrects the details only love would know. Emotional beat: bittersweet communion; authorship surrendered to the heart.

chapters.title: The Signature
chapters.summary: Rafael signs the memoir with her own name for the first time, publishing it independently with Camille. The book—about a woman who wrote everyone's life but her own—becomes a quiet phenomenon. Emotional beat: identity claimed; belonging earned, not granted.

chapters.title: The Vow, Kept Late
chapters.summary: Edmund's decline deepens. Rafael moves into the cliffside house as his companion, keeping the vow from the letter at last—not as a return to what was, but a stay through what is. Emotional beat: love against duty resolved; she stays not because she promised, but because she chooses.

chapters.title: Last Light on the Water
chapters.summary: Edmund's final lucid evening: he tells Rafael the memoir is the truest thing he never wrote, and asks her to write the next one in her own voice. He dies at dawn, at peace, her hand in his. POV Rafael. Emotional beat: grief arriving on schedule, love arriving on time.

chapters.title: First Person, Present Tense
chapters.summary: One year later. Rafael, in her own house above the same sea, begins a novel of her own—first person, present tense. Camille visits with proofs of Edmund's final poems. Rafael writes a dedication to the man who saw her clearly at last. Emotional beat: belonging found; the ghost becomes the author.
